A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and the appendices report original Gaussian-mixture simulations and LifeCLEF experiments measuring prediction-set size and coverage.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, with additional LifeCLEF results for naive multi-input calibration and APS scoring.

M1.justification: The randomized p-values, voting refinements, simulation algorithm and aggregation procedures in Sections 3–5 are retained. APS is tested as another nonconformity score within the existing general framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture task and LifeCLEF 2015 data, with Pl@ntNet-300K pretraining. Randomly grouped same-class images and naturally grouped user submissions were already evaluated in v1. The additions do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 and Table 2 newly evaluate class-conditional conformal prediction calibrated on averaged multi-input scores for LifeCLEF. The corresponding naive approach previously had only synthetic results. The existing aggregation comparators remain; Quantile and ScEnv are matched as label variants.

E3.justification: v2 adds LifeCLEF evaluation using randomized APS scores at temperatures 1 and 20, plus multi-input calibration evaluated by input-group size and across sizes. The stated splits, model configurations and settings of the original experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 and new Figure 8 test sensitivity to replacing softmax nonconformity scores with APS scores. Appendix B.2 extends the investigation of naive calibration failure to LifeCLEF. The existing synthetic analyses and exchangeability-violation experiment are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty shading to the existing LifeCLEF Figures 3 and 7 and reports +/- quantities in new Table 2. Synthetic repetition counts and uncertainty formulas are unchanged. The new LifeCLEF uncertainty quantities are not defined, and no additional run counts or seeds are documented.

E6.justification: The LifeCLEF result record is substantially revised and expanded. At temperature 20 and m=10, Figure 3's exchangeable-majority set size changes from roughly 270 to 60, while Figure 7's Wilcoxon coverage changes from about 0.895 to 0.962 under the same stated settings. New Table 2 reports average naive-baseline length 646 +/- 1 and coverage 91.9 +/- 0.3%; new Figure 8 supplies APS results. The PDFs do not explain the revisions to the retained curves.

T1.justification: New Remark 3.4 states that validity extends conditionally to varying input count m when exchangeability holds conditional on m. Appendix C also restores the missing majority threshold in its coverage-event expression. The principal theorems and proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: exact class-conditional p-value distributions, improved voting aggregation and smaller prediction sets through p-value aggregation under exchangeability.

C2.justification: v2 explains Beta-Binomial overcoverage through discrete quantiles and suggests further randomization. Appendix B.2 clarifies when calibration on complete multi-inputs could work and attributes its large sets primarily to insufficient calibration data. The existing limitations concerning dependent real multi-inputs remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 explicitly specifies the APS score, including its uniform random term, in Equation 24. This provides implementation information for the added experiment. Hardware, training-time and code-access statements are retained from v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Romano et al. (2020) for APS and Ding et al. (2025) for long-tailed conformal prediction. Section 2.1 changes the attribution of classwise conformal prediction from Vovk (2012) to Vovk et al. (2005). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: grammar and terminology corrections, new subdivisions B.1–B.2 and D.1–D.2, updated cross-references and a NeurIPS conference footer replacing the preprint footer. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and the APS Figure 8, changes Figure 3 to logarithmic size axes with a corrected caption, and adds shading and legend edits to retained plots. The former Figure 8 becomes Figure 9 with unchanged content. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The APS sensitivity experiment and quantified LifeCLEF naive baseline provide useful empirical checks absent from v1, while logarithmic size plots make the comparisons easier to inspect. These are limited gains: the dependent-input failure remains unresolved, and the new uncertainty quantities and substantial revisions to existing curves lack adequate explanation.
